papers.title: OPTIMIZING CLOUD RESOURCE ALLOCATION USING MULTI AGENT DEEP REINFORCEMENT LEARNING-BASED ADAPTIVE HHO ALGORITHM
papers.abstract: Cloud computing workloads are projected to grow by 23.1% annually, with over 80% of enterprises adopting multi-cloud strategies, creating a pressing need for optimal virtual machine (VM) resource allocation to ensure cost efficiency and performance. However, existing allocation strategies suffer from static optimization limitations and inefficient adaptation to dynamic workloads, leading to frequent resource underutilization and service delays. To address these issues, this work proposes a novel Multi-Agent Deep Reinforcement Learning-Based Adaptive Harris Hawks Optimization (MADRL-AHHO) algorithm for cloud resource allocation using the VM Resource Allocation dataset (VM-0 to VM-5 classes). Initially, the dataset is preprocessed through normalization and feature selection to reduce dimensionality and noise. Feature extraction is enhanced using a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) integrated with Firefly Optimization (CNN-FFO), which is benchmarked for learning capacity and solution convergence. However, performance limitations in CNN-FFO under dynamic load conditions are overcome by integrating CNN with Adaptive Harris Hawks Optimization (CNN-AHHO), which dynamically adjusts its exploration and exploitation capabilities based on multi-agent reinforcement feedback. The agents interact with the environment to learn optimal VM allocation policies by maximizing resource utilization and minimizing SLA violations. Experimental results demonstrate that CNN-AHHO outperforms CNN-FFO and traditional machine learning methods in terms of allocation accuracy, convergence rate, and computational efficiency, thereby offering a robust and adaptive solution for cloud infrastructure management.

papers.title: Transformer-Based Scalable Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning for Joint Resource Optimization in Cloud–Edge–End Video Streaming Systems
papers.abstract: Cloud-edge-end (CEE) collaboration has demonstrated significant potential in video streaming analysis. However, dynamic wireless environments, lack of incentive mechanisms, and constrained resources (e.g., transmission power, bandwidth, and computing resources) remain the primary bottlenecks for achieving efficient CEE-based video processing. To address these challenges, this paper focuses on a multi-user CEE scenario with dynamic wireless channels and investigates the joint optimization of adaptive incentives, cooperative offloading, and resource allocation. We propose a novel framework, called JROC, to motivate edge devices (EDs) to participate in collaborative computation within CEE, thereby enhancing system utility. Specifically, JROC encompasses a smart contract-based adaptive incentive mechanism and an Adaptive Transformer-based multi-agent reinforcement Learning Algorithm (ATLA). The incentive mechanism leverages blockchain to ensure trustworthy and automated incentive distribution, while ATLA captures long-term dependencies and global state features among agents to guide video tasks in dynamic environments through adaptive compression, cooperative offloading, and resource allocation. Moreover, we discuss key steps for deploying the proposed algorithm in a real CEE prototype, including lightweight actor inference at the terminal side and training at the edge. Experimental results based on a real-world operator dataset show that, compared to existing methods, JROC achieves higher long-term system utility while maintaining favorable scalability, thereby validating its effectiveness in resource-constrained and under-incentivized CEE video streaming scenarios.

papers.title: Mobility-Aware Resource Allocation for mmWave IAB Networks: A Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning Approach
papers.abstract: MmWaves have been envisioned as a promising direction to provide Gbps wireless access. However, they are susceptible to high path losses and blockages, which directional antennas can only partially mitigate. That makes mmWave networks coverage-limited, thus requiring dense deployments. Integrated access and backhaul (IAB) architectures have emerged as a cost-effective solution for network densification. Resource allocation in mmWave IAB networks must face big challenges to cope with heavy temporal dynamics, such as intermittent links caused by user mobility and blockages from moving obstacles. This makes it extremely difficult to find optimal and adaptive solutions. In this article, exploiting the distributed structure of the problem, we propose a Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (MARL) framework to optimize user throughput via flow routing and link scheduling in mmWave IAB networks characterized by user mobility and link outages generated by moving obstacles. The proposed approach implicitly captures the environment dynamics, coordinates the interference, and manages the buffer levels of IAB relay nodes. We design different MARL components, considering full-duplex and half-duplex IAB-nodes. In addition, we provide a communication and coordination scheme for RL agents in an online training framework, addressing the feasibility issues of practical systems. Numerical results show the effectiveness of the proposed approach.

papers.title: Efficient Resource Allocation for On-Demand Mobile-Edge Cloud Computing
papers.abstract: Mobile-edge cloud computing is a new paradigm to provide cloud computing capabilities at the edge of pervasive radio access networks in close proximity to mobile users. Aiming at provisioning flexible on-demand mobile-edge cloud service, in this paper we propose a comprehensive framework consisting of a resource-efficient computation offloading mechanism for users and a joint communication and computation (JCC) resource allocation mechanism for network operator. Specifically, we first study the resource-efficient computation offloading problem for a user, in order to reduce user's resource occupation by determining its optimal communication and computation resource profile with minimum resource occupation and meanwhile satisfying the QoS constraint. We then tackle the critical problem of user admission control for JCC resource allocation, in order to properly select the set of users for resource demand satisfaction. We show the admission control problem is NP-hard, and hence develop an efficient approximation solution of a low complexity by carefully designing the user ranking criteria and rigourously derive its performance guarantee. To prevent the manipulation that some users may untruthfully report their valuations in acquiring mobile-edge cloud service, we further resort to the powerful tool of critical value approach to design truthful pricing scheme for JCC resource allocation. Extensive performance evaluation demonstrates that the proposed schemes can achieve superior performance for on-demand mobile-edge cloud computing.

literature_themes.theme: Optimizing Resource Allocation in Cloud and Edge Computing Using Reinforcement Learning
literature_themes.summary: This cluster of papers explores various approaches to optimize resource allocation in cloud-based and mobile-edge computing environments using multi-agent reinforcement learning techniques. The studies propose novel algorithms and frameworks that address challenges such as dynamic workloads, resource underutilization, and performance inefficiencies in cloud resource management and video streaming systems. Key contributions include the development of adaptive algorithms that leverage deep reinforcement learning and incentive mechanisms to enhance system utility and user experience.
literature_themes.limitations: The papers highlight limitations related to static optimization strategies, performance issues under dynamic conditions, and the complexity of user admission control in resource allocation. Additionally, some approaches may not fully address the scalability of solutions in real-world applications or the integration of various resource types.
literature_themes.gap_relevance: This cluster identifies significant research gaps in the optimization of resource allocation strategies, particularly in adapting to dynamic environments and multi-user scenarios. It supports further investigation into hybrid models that combine reinforcement learning with other optimization techniques, as well as the development of incentive mechanisms to enhance user participation and system efficiency.

literature_themes.theme: Resource Allocation in mmWave IAB Networks Using MARL
literature_themes.summary: This cluster primarily investigates the challenges of resource allocation in mmWave Integrated Access and Backhaul (IAB) networks, particularly in the context of user mobility and link outages. It proposes a Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (MARL) framework to optimize user throughput by addressing flow routing and link scheduling, while effectively managing environmental dynamics and interference.
literature_themes.limitations: The proposed MARL framework may face limitations in scalability and adaptability to varying network conditions. Additionally, the reliance on simulations may not fully capture real-world complexities, such as varying user behaviors and unpredictable mobility patterns.
literature_themes.gap_relevance: This cluster highlights the need for advanced resource allocation strategies in mmWave networks, particularly under dynamic conditions, thus supporting research in adaptive network management and the development of more resilient communication systems.

summary: The retrieved literature on Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (MARL) for dynamic resource allocation in cloud computing reveals two primary themes: optimizing resource allocation in cloud and edge environments, and addressing resource challenges in mmWave IAB networks. While various novel algorithms and frameworks have been proposed to enhance system utility and user experience, limitations such as static optimization strategies and scalability issues persist. The studies highlight significant research gaps in adapting to dynamic conditions and multi-user scenarios, emphasizing the need for hybrid models and adaptive solutions to improve resource management efficiency.
scholarly_positioning: Existing research on Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (MARL) for resource allocation in cloud computing predominantly focuses on static optimization strategies, which fail to adapt to the dynamic workloads and user behaviors prevalent in real-world applications. While some studies propose novel algorithms, they often overlook the complexities of multi-user scenarios and the integration of various resource types, leading to scalability issues. Furthermore, the reliance on simulation-based evaluations limits the applicability of these approaches in practical settings. This proposed research aims to bridge these gaps by developing a hybrid MARL framework that incorporates adaptive algorithms and incentive mechanisms, thereby enhancing resource allocation efficiency in dynamic environments and contributing to the broader discourse on resilient cloud computing systems.
research_scope: This study will investigate the effectiveness of a hybrid Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (MARL) framework for dynamic resource allocation in cloud computing environments, specifically targeting cloud-based deep learning applications. The evaluation period will span six months, during which the framework will be tested against traditional optimization algorithms and existing MARL frameworks in simulated cloud environments. The primary outcomes will include resource allocation efficiency and system utility, while secondary outcomes will focus on user satisfaction metrics and scalability performance. The study will also assess the impact of adaptive algorithms and incentive mechanisms on user participation, providing insights into their effectiveness in real-world scenarios. By addressing the limitations of static optimization strategies and scalability issues, this research aims to enhance the resilience and efficiency of resource management in dynamic cloud computing contexts.

technical_feasibility: The study requires access to simulated cloud computing environments and real-world workload traces for data sources. It does not require open-source model access, hidden state extraction, or labelled datasets. However, it may benefit from GPU resources for running simulations and training the MARL framework. Since the study focuses on user satisfaction metrics, it may also require human participants for validation of user experience and trust calibration measures. To address this, the research design should include a human-subject component to gather user feedback on satisfaction and trust in the resource allocation process.
gap: Prior studies have demonstrated the potential of Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (MARL) to optimize resource allocation in cloud computing environments; however, they treat user behaviors and dynamic workloads as static, leaving unclear whether adaptive algorithms can significantly enhance resource allocation efficiency and user satisfaction in real-world scenarios. This matters practically because effective resource management is critical for the performance of cloud-based applications, especially under varying user demands. Therefore, this study investigates the effectiveness of a hybrid MARL framework that incorporates adaptive algorithms and incentive mechanisms for dynamic resource allocation in cloud-based deep learning applications.
question: How does the implementation of a hybrid Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning framework, incorporating adaptive algorithms and incentive mechanisms, improve resource allocation efficiency and user satisfaction in dynamic cloud-based deep learning applications compared to traditional optimization algorithms and existing MARL frameworks?
theoretical_mechanism: The proposed research investigates the impact of a hybrid Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (MARL) framework (independent variable) on resource allocation efficiency and user satisfaction (dependent variables) in dynamic cloud-based deep learning applications. The adaptive algorithms and incentive mechanisms serve as mediators that enhance the responsiveness of resource allocation to fluctuating user demands and behaviors. The theoretical framework is grounded in systems theory, where the causal chain posits that improved resource allocation efficiency leads to higher system utility, while user satisfaction is influenced by perceived responsiveness and engagement. Assumptions requiring empirical validation include the effectiveness of adaptive algorithms in real-time scenarios and the influence of incentive mechanisms on user participation. System-level outcomes are mediated by technical mechanisms such as real-time resource monitoring and allocation adjustments, while user-level outcomes are mediated by psychological mechanisms like perceived responsiveness and engagement.
hypothesis: Implementing a hybrid Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning framework with adaptive algorithms and incentive mechanisms will significantly improve resource allocation efficiency compared to traditional optimization algorithms, with the mediating effect of user engagement leading to higher user satisfaction in dynamic cloud-based deep learning applications.

proposal: This research proposal aims to develop a novel hybrid Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (MARL) framework specifically designed for dynamic resource allocation in cloud-based deep learning applications. Unlike existing approaches that primarily rely on static optimization strategies, this study addresses critical limitations such as scalability and adaptability to fluctuating user demands and behaviors, which have been inadequately explored in prior literature. The proposed framework integrates adaptive algorithms and incentive mechanisms, positing that these elements will enhance resource allocation efficiency and user satisfaction through real-time responsiveness. The research question posits: How does the implementation of this hybrid MARL framework improve resource allocation efficiency and user satisfaction compared to traditional optimization algorithms and existing MARL frameworks? The theoretical mechanism suggests that adaptive algorithms will mediate the relationship between the hybrid framework and improved outcomes by enabling real-time adjustments to resource allocation, while incentive mechanisms will foster user engagement, thereby enhancing satisfaction. Constructs will be operationalized through measurable variables such as throughput and latency for resource allocation efficiency, and user satisfaction will be assessed via validated surveys. The methodology includes robust experimental design with controls for fixed workload scenarios and variable user behavior simulations, ensuring comprehensive evaluation against established baselines. Statistical analyses will employ ANOVA and regression techniques to validate findings, while potential confounding variables will be addressed through sensitivity analyses. The study will span six months, utilizing simulated cloud environments and real-world workload traces, with a focus on user engagement to ensure practical relevance. Expected contributions include theoretical advancements in integrating adaptive algorithms and incentive mechanisms within MARL, empirical findings on their effectiveness, and practical deployment guidelines for real-world applications, ultimately filling a critical gap in the literature regarding dynamic user behaviors in cloud computing.

The background highlights the limitations of existing static optimization strategies and scalability issues in current MARL frameworks, establishing a scholarly positioning that emphasizes the need for adaptive solutions. The literature reveals a critical empirical gap regarding the effectiveness of adaptive algorithms in real-world scenarios, leading to the research question: How does the implementation of a hybrid MARL framework, incorporating adaptive algorithms and incentive mechanisms, improve resource allocation efficiency and user satisfaction in dynamic cloud-based deep learning applications compared to traditional optimization algorithms and existing MARL frameworks?
